:::{#def-image}
#### Image

The **image** of a [function](#def-function) $f : A \to B$
is the set of values that $f$ actually takes:

$$f(A) \eqdef \set{f(a) : a \in A}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-image-range}
#### Image and range

Many sources call the image the **range**,
but others use "range" for the codomain,
so these notes avoid "range" for functions in general
(see [Wikipedia: Range of a function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_of_a_function)).
For example, for $f : \reals \to \reals$ with $f(a) = a^2$,
"the range of $f$" could mean the image $[0, \infty)$
or the codomain $\reals$.

The image is always a subset of the codomain,
because every value $f(a)$ lies in $B$.

:::
